memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Their father Jacob said to them, 'You have deprived me of my children. Joseph is no more and Simeon is no more, and now you want to take Benjamin. Everything is against me!'" - Gen 42:36 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jacob sinks into despair. Believing Joseph dead, with Simeon now held in Egypt and a demand that Benjamin be sent too, he cries out, "Everything is against me!" From where Jacob stood, it truly looked that way — loss piled on loss, threat upon threat, with no relief in sight.

But here is the striking thing: Jacob was completely wrong. In reality, nothing was against him. Joseph was not dead but alive and ruling Egypt. Simeon was not lost but safe, and would soon be restored. The demand for Benjamin was not a disaster but the very path that would reunite the whole family and save them from famine. Everything Jacob thought was against him was actually part of God working for him.

How often do we make Jacob's mistake? In our darkest moments, we survey our troubles and conclude, "Everything is against me." We add up the losses and the fears and decide that God has abandoned us or that life is set against us. Yet, like Jacob, we see only part of the picture. What feels like ruin may be rescue in disguise.

The New Testament turns Jacob's despairing words completely around: "If God is for us, who can be against us?" (Rom 8:31). For those who love God, "all things work together for good" (Rom 8:28). When you are tempted to cry, "Everything is against me," remember that you cannot see the whole story. The God who was working for Jacob when it all seemed against him is working for you too.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When have I concluded "everything is against me" while seeing only part of the story?
2. Do I trust that God is working for me even when it seems otherwise?
3. How does Romans 8:28 reframe my current troubles?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when I cry "everything is against me," remind me that I see only part of the story. You are for me, working all things for my good. Help me to trust You in the dark. Amen.
